classification: Synthetic crop-model-v2 reducer-state software fixture; not a crop benchmark or candidate comparison
contract: For the same frozen tomato thermal profile, explicit cold/warm synthetic weather series at two location tags must change reducer thermal state according to the single-sine source method while retaining the same frozen source target range. For each of the four weather cases, a five-day short-horizon run and ten-day run sharing the exact same first five daily environments must show no target or thermal-progress normalization to the supplied run window. A paired A-warm ten-day control varying only RunConfig.meanDailyGddC from 0 to 14 must retain identical v2 target range and thermal progress fields (gddAccumC and biomassFrac); it does not claim independence in unrelated v2 calculations or test/change v1 compatibility.

commonDailyFields.dateSequence: 2026-10-01 through 2026-10-10, one UTC calendar day per tick; the five-day series is the first five dates.
commonDailyFields.otherFields: Hold identical across all runs; no irrigation, weather interventions, or location-derived values.

method.dailyThermalEquation: Daily units = max(0, mean temperature above 7.2°C by single-sine horizontal cutoff minus mean temperature above 33.3°C by the same method).
method.accumulationEquation: gddAccumC(day n) = sum of the first n daily thermal units; the v2 reducer caps only at the frozen maximum target 1117°C·days.
method.developmentRangeEquation: thermalDevelopmentRange = [gddAccumC/1117, gddAccumC/1024]; the reducer stores biomassFrac as the conservative lower value gddAccumC/1117.
method.windowRule: Never derive or rescale either target endpoint from a run's mean temperature, duration, or accumulated thermal total. Reuse the same frozen modelInputs for both horizon lengths.

assertions: For each of the four weather cases, the five-day state from the short run matches the state after the same five-day prefix reduced from the ten-day run for gddAccumC and biomassFrac.
The thermal target remains exactly [1024,1117] in both horizons.
The ten-day gddAccumC and biomassFrac match the frozen case expectations.

meanDailyGddCIndependenceControl.purpose: Register a check that the crop-model-v2 fixed target range and thermal progress fields (gddAccumC and biomassFrac) are independent of the legacy RunConfig.meanDailyGddC field and use frozen v2 thermal parameters plus daily Tmin/Tmax.
assertions: Both configs use the exact same ten-day A-warm 18/30°C weather series and exact same frozen v2 modelInputs.
Only meanDailyGddC differs; both reducer states match expected values and each other at day 5 and day 10 within the registered tolerances.
The target range remains exactly [1024,1117] in both runs.
This checks independence of the v2 target range and thermal progress fields only; it makes no claim about unrelated v2 calculations and neither tests nor changes crop-model-v1 compatibility.

biomassFrac.basis: Division by the fixed 1117°C·day upper target only.

tolerances.targetRange: Exact structural equality to [1024,1117] °C·days; no numeric tolerance.
tolerances.prefixControl: Compare gddAccumC and biomassFrac using their bounds above; frozen input identity and day counts are exact.

assumptions: The two location tags are labels for explicit synthetic forcing and do not stand for real coordinates or local weather records.
The same frozen crop and thermal modelInputs are reused across all four weather cases and both horizons.
Neutral synthetic production and root-zone inputs exist only to satisfy the v2 reducer replay gate; thermal state is the only crop state under evaluation.
All weather days are constant within each ten-day series, and the five-day horizon is the exact prefix of that series.
missingInputs: Cultivar-specific mapping of the four OSU Table 6 values.
Measured daily weather and site coordinates for either synthetic location.
Source-backed tomato production and root-zone parameter sets.
Independent measured or reference-model outcome data and a held-out comparison design.
evidenceBoundary: Synthetic reducer-state software behavior only. This fixture cannot establish tomato/cultivar accuracy, biological validity, transfer across climates, measured or reference-model agreement, or predictive performance.
